slides.title: Strategy pages

items.text: Increase adoption and channel mix across the base.

items.title: Scale product

items.title: Optimise unit cost
items.text: Automate and simplify delivery.

points: Ensure there are no red flags
Plan the pilot in detail and prepare to start

slides.soWhat: Purchase is the only stage without a named success metric today; add win rate to the dashboard.

slides.title: Improvement runs as a five-step cycle that repeats every quarter

items.label: Measure
items.text: Baseline the metric

items.label: Diagnose
items.text: Find the root cause

items.label: Design
items.text: Choose the fix

items.label: Pilot
items.text: Test on one site

items.label: Scale
items.text: Roll out and lock in

items.label: Optimise

exhibit.foundation: One customer data platform and a single pricing engine

slides.soWhat: New segments carry half the growth and none of the current capability; fund that pillar first.

slides.soWhat: Option B pays back its extra $2M of capex within its first year of run-cost savings.

weaknesses: Two regions without a country lead

right.heading: From 2027

Hiring within budget needs no group sign-off

slides.title: Three value propositions, each with proof from the last two years

rows.label: Functional expertise
rows.text: Fourteen commercial-excellence projects in the sector since 2024, including two for direct competitors.

rows.label: Local network
rows.text: Offices in all three target markets with partners who have run the regulator conversations before.

rows.label: Delivery track record
rows.text: Every engagement since 2023 delivered on the agreed date with the agreed team.

slides.soWhat: The network is the differentiator: no other bidder has partners in all three markets.

slides.title: The core team brings sector, technology and change experience
slides.soWhat: All four have worked together on a live migration; the team needs no forming time.

slides.title: Four capabilities carry the go-to-market plan

items.title: Market insight
items.text: Segment sizing, buyer research and win-loss analysis.

items.title: Demand generation
items.text: Campaigns, content and events tied to pipeline targets.

items.title: Partner channel
items.text: Two resellers per region with joint plans.

items.title: Revenue operations
items.text: Pipeline hygiene, forecasting and pricing control.

slides.soWhat: Revenue operations is the one capability nobody owns today; appoint the lead before the campaign launch.

slides.title: Three entry countries, three different reasons to go

items.title: Germany
items.text: The largest market in the region and the slowest to enter.

items.title: Belgium
items.text: The smallest market and the fastest proof of the playbook.
points: Language coverage from the Dutch team

items.title: Netherlands
items.text: The most digital market, with a gap left by a competitor's exit.

slides.soWhat: Belgium first: it proves the playbook in six months at a tenth of the German cost.

slides.title: The Growth plan doubles seats at a lower cost per seat

items.title: Starter
items.text: Per seat per month, up to 10 seats

items.title: Growth
items.text: Per seat per month, 11 to 100 seats

items.title: Enterprise
items.text: Annual contract, dedicated support

slides.soWhat: Move the 40 accounts sitting at 10 seats onto Growth; each one is a price cut that pays for itself in expansion.
